settings.heading: A house, not a factory
settings.text: We began with one printing table in Chandpol Bazaar in 1974. Fifty years later we still print by hand — we simply have more tables, and more families around them.
settings.caption: Since 1974

settings.heading: Fifty years of keeping a craft alive
settings.text: From one printing table to forty artisan families across three states.
settings.footer_text: The next fifty start with the makers we train today.

settings.title: One table, two blocks
settings.text: Kala Devi begins printing lengths of cotton from a single table behind her family’s shop in Chandpol Bazaar.

settings.title: The first workshop
settings.text: Four printers join Kala Devi and the house moves into its own courtyard in Bagru.

settings.title: Natural dyes only
settings.text: Every synthetic pigment leaves the workshop. The indigo vats are rebuilt from scratch.

settings.title: Brass, clay and wood
settings.text: We begin working with casters in Moradabad and potters in Khurja.

settings.title: Forty families, one standard
settings.text: Kala Katha now trains twelve apprentices a year and repairs anything it has ever sold.

settings.heading: Nine passes of indigo
settings.text: Watch a length of cloth move from raw cotton to finished indigo in forty seconds.
settings.caption: Filmed in Bagru, Rajasthan

settings.title: Bagru — block printing
settings.text: Nine families, eleven tables, one indigo vat that has never been allowed to die.

settings.title: Moradabad — brass casting
settings.text: Sand-cast, hand-finished, and left unlacquered so it ages with you.

settings.title: Khurja — pottery
settings.text: Thrown on the wheel and fired twice, for glazes that do not craze.

settings.quote: The cloth remembers the hand that printed it.
settings.author: Ramesh Chhipa

settings.heading: Slow-made objects for everyday rituals
settings.text: Everything we sell can be repaired, re-dyed or re-blocked by the family that made it. That is the whole business model.
